claims.text: Adding 1–2 wt.% Y2O3 during powder-metallurgy processing of NbMoTaW, with high-energy ball milling and spark plasma sintering at 1200°C, will produce a uniform dispersion of Y2O3 nanoparticles.
Uniformly dispersed Y2O3 nanoparticles will act as sinks for radiation-induced defects in NbMoTaW.
The Y2O3 nanoparticles will capture radiation-induced vacancies.
The Y2O3 nanoparticles will capture radiation-induced interstitials.
Defect capture by Y2O3 nanoparticles will suppress the growth of extended defect clusters.
Suppression of extended defect clusters will mitigate irradiation-induced swelling.
Y2O3 nanoparticle pinning will maintain or improve the mechanical strength of NbMoTaW.
At approximately 500°C under ion irradiation, Y2O3-modified NbMoTaW will have lower defect density than unmodified NbMoTaW.
At approximately 500°C under ion irradiation, Y2O3-modified NbMoTaW will have lower volumetric swelling than unmodified NbMoTaW.
The yield strength of irradiated Y2O3-modified NbMoTaW will be at least comparable to that of the unmodified baseline.
The hardness of irradiated Y2O3-modified NbMoTaW will be at least comparable to that of the unmodified baseline.
Ion irradiation at approximately 500°C simulates fusion plasma-facing conditions.
The predicted benefits depend on maintaining a uniform and stable Y2O3 nanoparticle dispersion.
Significant deviations in processing parameters or oxide-dispersion quality may negate the radiation-tolerance and mechanical benefits.
